subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What best describes an iterative design strategy?
options: Producing a single final design straight away with no changes
A repeating cycle of designing, making, testing and evaluating to refine a solution
Letting the manufacturer decide the design
questions.explain: Iterative design is a continuous loop of design, model, test and evaluate, with each cycle refining the outcome.

questions.q: In user-centred design (UCD), who is placed at the centre of the design process?
options: The end user of the product
questions.explain: User-centred design keeps the needs and wants of the end user at the heart of every stage of designing.

questions.q: A designer builds a card model, tests it with users, changes the shape, remodels and tests again. Which strategy is this?
questions.explain: Repeated cycles of modelling, testing and refining are the defining feature of an iterative approach.

questions.q: What is meant by a collaborative approach to designing?
options: Working entirely alone with no input
Working with others such as clients, users and specialists to develop ideas
Making the product before designing it
questions.explain: Collaboration draws on the skills and views of a team, client and stakeholders to improve the design.

questions.q: Why would a user-centred designer collect anthropometric data before designing a chair?
options: To decide the selling price of the chair
To ensure the chair's dimensions suit the sizes of the intended users
questions.explain: Anthropometric data on human body measurements helps make products that physically fit and suit their users.

questions.q: A team of designers, engineers and a client meet regularly to combine their expertise on a new appliance. Which strategy best describes this?
questions.explain: Bringing together different people and their expertise to develop a product is a collaborative strategy.

questions.q: In isometric drawing, at what angle to the horizontal are the two receding base lines normally drawn?
questions.explain: Isometric drawings use vertical lines plus lines at 30 degrees to the horizontal to show a 3D view.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation CAD stand for?
questions.explain: CAD stands for Computer-Aided Design, the use of software to create and edit designs.

questions.q: Which is a genuine advantage of using CAD rather than hand drawing?
options: Designs can be easily edited, saved and shared, and viewed from different angles
It removes the need to understand the design
It always produces the finished physical product automatically
questions.explain: CAD lets designers quickly modify, store, render and share accurate drawings and rotate 3D models.

questions.q: How many vanishing points does a one-point perspective drawing use?
questions.explain: One-point perspective has a single vanishing point on the horizon towards which lines converge.

questions.q: What is orthographic projection mainly used to communicate?
options: A colourful marketing render of a product
Accurate 2D working drawings showing front, plan and side views with dimensions
The user's opinions of a product
questions.explain: Orthographic projection gives dimensioned 2D views (front, plan and end) used as working drawings for manufacture.

questions.q: What does an exploded diagram show?
options: The product being destroyed for testing
How the separate parts of a product fit and assemble together
The selling price of each component
questions.explain: An exploded view separates the components along their assembly lines to show how they fit together.

questions.q: A designer wants a sketch that clearly shows the surface texture and material of a product to a client. Which technique is most suitable?
questions.explain: Rendering adds tone, colour and texture so a drawing realistically shows the intended materials and finish.

questions.q: You must show a customer, step by step, how to assemble a flat-pack shelf. Which drawing type is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Exploded diagrams clearly show the order and position in which separate parts fit together during assembly.

questions.q: In the ACCESS FM specification checklist, what does the letter 'F' stand for?
questions.explain: In ACCESS FM, F stands for Function - what the product must do and how it must perform.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a design specification?
options: To list the exact machine settings for the factory
To set out the criteria a successful design must meet
To record the profit made from sales
questions.explain: A design specification states the measurable requirements and criteria that the final design should satisfy.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of objective testing of a prototype?
options: Asking a user whether they like the colour
Measuring the load in newtons a shelf can hold before it bends
Recording how attractive people find the shape
Noting a client's personal preference for the style
questions.explain: Objective testing produces measurable, fact-based data such as a recorded load, rather than personal opinion.

questions.q: Against what should a finished prototype primarily be evaluated?
options: The designer's original mood board only
The points in the design specification
The price of a competitor's advertising
questions.explain: Evaluation checks the outcome against each criterion in the specification to judge how successful it is.

questions.q: A specification states a torch must weigh under 200 g. Testing shows it weighs 260 g. What is the correct evaluation conclusion for this criterion?
options: It fails this criterion and the design needs modifying
The torch is perfect as it is
questions.explain: At 260 g the torch exceeds the 200 g limit, so it fails this measurable criterion and requires refinement.

questions.q: What does a manufacturing (production) specification mainly provide?
options: The precise details, dimensions and tolerances needed to make the product
questions.explain: A manufacturing specification gives the exact measurements, materials and tolerances so the product can be made accurately.
